entries.title: Vendored review-skill runtime (three-strikes design review, cond-0024)
entries.body: Four issues (0017/0019/0023/0024) came from the review skill trusting `python3` off an uncontrolled PATH while Codex workers hop between exec environments. Make the skill own its interpreter: uv-managed project env inside the skill dir (`uv run --project "$SKILL_DIR"` everywhere), deleting the whole machine-level-pip mitigation pile. Skillshare-owned change — Colin's call on the exact shape.

entries.title: Post-shakedown pruning pass
entries.body: The shakedown proved which surfaces matter; delete what it never exercised (dead flags, unused config keys, leftover v1 language in profiles/docs). Complexity should end the shakedown *lower* than it started. Shape: one sweep, guided by "was this touched in the campaign evidence?", with the coherence lints as the safety net.

entries.body: (terminal touch-scroll; output-pipeline reattach on restart) so the fork can retire to a thin pin. Both are self-contained, regression-safe, genuinely useful upstream. Shape: two PRs from the prepared texts in `docs/fork/`, then rebase the deploy branch per upstream release. Gate: Colin's go on opening PRs.

entries.title: Session-env durability across cao-server restarts
entries.body: The in-memory session env store is the last restart casualty (shim PATH/ZDOTDIR lost; bounce guard exists only because of it). Shape: small fork patch persisting session env_vars to the DB and re-applying on startup — which would let us DELETE the bounce guard entirely (a net-complexity win, the best kind of fix).

entries.title: Generation-bound harness session operations
entries.body: The new `harness-session-compaction` and `harness-route-switching` skills define safe cross-provider behavior, but current CAO direct input is not idle- or generation-bound and interactive model menus require state-aware selection. Add one narrow conductor operation that validates terminal generation and durable checkpoint, sends literal slash commands/keys without bracketed-paste mode, matches rendered menu labels rather than arrow counts, attests the result with provider-native status, and writes append-only compact/route receipts. This should delete operator-only compaction and model-fallback procedures.

entries.title: `conduct deploy`
entries.body: One command: version bump, `uv tool install --reinstall` (both tools + plugin), content-marker verification, doctor drift check, optional server bounce with identity re-record. Today this is procedure-by-discipline; cond-0009 taught us discipline decays at 3am.

entries.title: Cross-campaign quota arbitration
entries.body: When dnd + aegix + mobile run concurrently, per-spawn preflight is local; nothing arbitrates globally. Shape: a small shared budget file written by a periodic all-provider quota snapshot; `conduct spawn` consults it and defers spawns per a policy concurrency weight. No new process — piggyback on spawn + sentinel tick.

entries.title: Durable supervisor-poke visibility (cond-0021)
entries.body: Record supervisor-to-worker MCP inbox pokes in campaign evidence so spec revisions and other persistent- worker steering are auditable. Prefer the smallest durable event-log fix. A full `conduct status --timeline` is optional only if it proves to be the simplest coherent solution rather than a broader monitoring redesign.

entries.title: Supervisor context lifecycle
entries.body: Terra ran PR01 down to ~19% context. Rather than trusting unbounded compaction: planned handover at PR boundaries when context < N% — journal checkpoint, spawn a fresh supervisor terminal seeded from journal + policy + `conduct lease list`, retire the old one. Shape: conducting-protocols guidance + a `conduct revive --handover` variant. Reward: campaign quality stops degrading with campaign length. Intentionally deferred from the 2026-07-21 self-heal readiness campaign by lead direction.

entries.body: Monitoring is mobile-first now; steering still needs SSH. Shape: OpenClaw bot command → `conduct tell`/`conduct approve` bridge over the existing foundry link (reply "approve merge-pr03" in Discord/Telegram and it lands as the gate approval). Reward: fully hands-off approvals from the beach, completing the original vision.

entries.title: Visual-QA baseline library
entries.body: Persist each PR's accepted screenshots as baselines; subsequent QA runs diff against them (structural/pixel-region diffs) before judgment. Reward: faster re-QA, objective regression evidence, and the persistent-QA reuse pattern gets a durable memory that survives terminal retirement.

entries.title: Memory-candidate adjudication pipeline — promoted to the pre-chess lifecycle track
entries.body: Workers emit `memory_candidate` blocks, but durable adjudication is not implemented yet. `docs/orchestration-defaults.md` now defines a persistent, sole-writer memory curator, merge-gated promotion, and role-calibrated recall. The same pre-chess track now includes durable, read-only PR review-wave history so a supervisor can compare the current count with optional human N-cycle guidance without a hard platform gate. This remains incomplete until retained rounds, review-history accounting, curator routing, provider capability checks, and focused integration tests land. Reward: campaigns stop relearning the same project facts without making memory an unreviewed source of truth.

entries.title: Skill-harvest loop
entries.body: Pipeline converting fire-marshal postmortems, friction analysis, Prime Agent `harness_state.json`, and repeat incident signatures into reviewed PRs against `cao-conductor/skills/` and `~/.config/skillshare/skills/`. The promotion rubric already exists in `docs/operational-skill-strategy.md`; this would give it an automated feed. Mostly *not* Prime-Agent-specific — it is a pipeline design. Depends on the friction analysis for its first real cargo.

entries.title: Route validation via Prime Lab
entries.body: Build a verifiers environment scoring a task type we actually run, then sweep it across providers *and* reasoning efforts to replace the prose intuition in the `route-ai-work` skill with measurement. Broader than CAO. Key motivation: model and effort do not decompose — Opus-5 can perform *worse* at higher reasoning effort on tasks it overthinks, while still being the correct model over a weaker one. That non-monotonic interaction cannot be reasoned to; it has to be measured as a 2-D surface per task type. Caveat: environment authoring is the real work and a bad environment yields confident garbage.

entries.title: `multi-agent-pr-review` depth-2 branch
entries.body: Prime Agent enforces `rlmMaxDepth` (default 1, runtime-settable, 0 is legal). At depth 2 a reviewer can spawn its own per-finding verifiers — a find-then-adversarially-verify topology the current stack cannot express, since Claude Code subagents have no Agent tool and CAO workers are recursion-gated. Not a rewrite of the working skill; a separate branch to explore the new topology.
